newsitem.title: UK: Scattered rain in UK farming areas, impact limited.
newsitem.headline: Scattered rain in UK farming areas, impact limited.

text.p: Scattered rains fell in eastern farming areas of the UK on Monday and overnight, but their impact on parched crops will be small, farming and weather analysts said on Tuesday.
"It's not enough to break any drought," a spokesman for the London Weather Centre said.
Showers rather than sustained rains fell, and their variability meant the extent of rainfall was hard to gauge, he said.

Between 1800 GMT Monday and 0600 GMT on Tuesday the highest rainfall had been reported at Norwich, with two millimetres, while the highest reported rainfall in eastern England during the day on Monday was at a weather station on the Norfolk coast, which reported four millimetres.
"With showers the amount may vary in between the reporting stations," the spokesman stressed. "There may have been more in other places," he said.
"That's not going to do any good," was the response of one farming source in East Anglia to reported rain levels.
Windy conditions in many areas had tended to minimise the beneficial effects of the rain by drying out soil and crops quickly, she said.
Despite the dry weather, many crops were developing well, she said. "People are very surprised how well things like sugar beet have germinated, given how dry the soil is."
In some areas, cold nights had been more worrying. "Sugar beet and peas need a warm seed bed," she said.
